classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicitly requested Pythagorean method on the marked unit triangle, approximate √2, and recognise its supplied number-line position as real.

spec.description: Unshaded horizontal number line with integer labels −3 to 3, origin point O, equal-leg right triangle above the interval from 0 to 1, vertex P_1, vertical length 1, double equality marks, right-angle marker and a compass arc from P_1 to the positive number line. A number-line template cannot express the attached triangle and compass construction.
spec.mathematics: O=(0,0), A=(1,0), P_1=(1,1). Both perpendicular legs have length 1. The arc is centred at O with radius sqrt(2), intersecting the positive number line at sqrt(2).
spec.answerVisibility: The triangle, labels, equality marks, right-angle marker and compass arc are permanent givens. No numerical hypotenuse answer is printed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to calculate the length of $OP_1$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using a pair of compasses, with point at $O$, the location of $\sqrt{2}$ on the number line has been accurately marked. What is the approximate value of $\sqrt{2}$? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

children.label: c
children.prompt: $\sqrt{2}$ can be placed on a number line. Is it a real number?

answer.worked: Yes. It has a position on the number line, so it is a real number.
